provenance: LLM-backend-derived (this session, no API key) + deterministic-checked — NOT a ship typology config. build_rec follows the cover×data matrix (build_rec_category); every indicator's flag is quote-grounded (verbatim) in the source md within the red-flag region (Phase 16). Coverage/data values are ILLUSTRATIVE (vision demo). FinCEN Alert, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).

indicators.flag: A	customer	intending	to	file	their	BOI	directly	with	FinCEN	makes	an	online	payment.
indicators.red_flag: Online payment for a self-file FinCEN BOI submission (free direct-filing channel)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A	customer	makes	an	online	payment	to	file	their	BOI	with	a	third-party	filing	company	or service	provider	through	a	website	domain	that	is	registered	in	a	foreign	location.
indicators.red_flag: BOI-filing payment to foreign-registered third-party domain (cross-border filing-service funnel)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: A	customer	sends	a	payment	to	file	their	BOI	through	a	third-party	filing	company	or	service provider	with	little	to	no	online	presence	or	a	name	similar	to	legitimate	companies	or government	entities.
indicators.red_flag: BOI-filing payee with no web footprint or government-lookalike name (impostor-payee screening)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: A	customer	uncharacteristically	sends	a	payment	to	a	counterparty	and	tells	the	financial institution	that	the	funds	must	be	sent	immediately	to	FinCEN	or	risk	a	fine,	penalty,	or	legal action	for	failure	to	file	their	BOI.
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-pattern urgent payment under BOI fine/penalty coercion (urgency-pressure scam tell)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag behavioural patterns consistent with scam victimization or vulnerable-customer exploitation â out-of-pattern payments to new beneficiaries, escalating transfer sequences to investment or romance-typed payees â escalating when the customer falls in a vulnerable segment.
build_logic.window: rolling 30 days per emerging payee relationship
build_logic.source: payment ledger + customer vulnerability segment + payee risk reference
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â fraud/AML & customer-protection review gate

indicators.flag: A	company	announces	its	“license”	or	“approval”	from	FinCEN	as	an	MSB	via	a	press	release through	a	news	wire	service,	on	its	website,	or	social	media.
indicators.red_flag: Public claim of FinCEN MSB "license/approval" via press wire or social media (false-endorsement OSINT)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: A	company	has	been	flagged	by	a	state	financial	regulator	as	potentially	fraudulent	or	for	having exploited	victims	in	the	past.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty flagged fraudulent by a state financial regulator (regulator-watchlist hit)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C18 (Sanctions / watchlist screening).

indicators.flag: A	company	is	registered	as	an	MSB	with	FinCEN	but	is	not	licensed	as	an	MSB	with	any	U.S. state	or	territorial	financial	regulatory	authority	where	they	claim	to	operate.
indicators.red_flag: MSB FinCEN-registered but unlicensed in its claimed operating state (registration-vs-license mismatch)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C13 (Account-opening / KYC risk profiling).

indicators.flag: A	company	with	a	limited	online	presence	prominently	highlights	their	MSB	registration	with FinCEN	or	claims	to	be	licensed	by	FinCEN	alongside	unverified	testimonials	and	promotions	of risk-free	high-investment	returns,	often	on	its	website,	a	news	wire	service,	or	a	social	media	post.
indicators.red_flag: Thin-web MSB touting FinCEN registration with risk-free high-return promises (investment-fraud OSINT)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: An	MSB	registered	with	FinCEN	shares	a	street	address	with	other	recently	registered	MSBs.
indicators.red_flag: Shared street address across recently registered MSBs (clustered-registration shell network)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D10 (Customer & account reference / entity-resolution data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: VASPs	or	other	financial	institutions	provide	a	user	with	a	virtual	currency	deposit	address	that has	been	flagged	as	potentially	fraudulent	by	blockchain	explorers	or	blockchain	analytic	tools.
indicators.red_flag: VC deposit address flagged fraudulent by blockchain analytics (on-chain risk-address screening)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: An	MSB	claims	that	its	AML	Program	or	“know	your	customer”	policies,	procedures,	or internal	controls	have	been	formally	approved	or	otherwise	vetted	by	FinCEN.
indicators.red_flag: Claim that FinCEN "approved/vetted" the MSB's AML program (false-vetting endorsement claim)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: An	individual	or	entity	claims	that	their	MSB	registration	with	FinCEN	is	either	a “recommendation,”	“certification	of	legitimacy,”	“approval,”	or	“endorsement”	by	FinCEN, Treasury,	or	the	U.S.	government,	or	any	U.S.	government	official.
indicators.red_flag: Registration recast as a FinCEN/Treasury "endorsement" of legitimacy (false-government-endorsement claim)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: An	individual	or	entity	claims	that	their	MSB	registration	with	FinCEN	equates	to	U.S. government	approval	to	operate	in	the	United	States.
indicators.red_flag: Registration claimed as U.S.-government operating approval (false-authority-to-operate claim)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: An	MSB	suggests	that	users	need	to	pay	an	 AML-related	processing	“fee”	or	a	“FinCEN	fee” to	use	its	services,	including	to	deposit	or	withdraw	funds	from	its	platform.
indicators.red_flag: MSB charging a bogus "FinCEN/AML fee" to deposit or withdraw (advance-fee shakedown)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A	company	is	registered	as	an	MSB	with	the	same	or	very	similar	name	of	a	large,	well-known financial	institution	that	appears	to	lack	an	MSB	registration	requirement,	such	as	a	bank, credit	union,	or	broker-dealer,	and	appears	to	have	no	official	affiliation	with	that	large,	well-known	financial	institution.
indicators.red_flag: MSB name impersonating a major bank/credit-union with no affiliation (lookalike-name impersonation)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C13 (Account-opening / KYC risk profiling).

indicators.flag: A	customer	sends	a	payment	purportedly	to	FinCEN	or	in	connection	with	an	apparent	penalty owed	to	FinCEN,	with	the	memo	line	denoting	“tax,”	“fee,”	“debt,”	“prize,”	“lien,”	or	“grant.”
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A	customer	uncharacteristically	sends	payments	to	a	new	counterparty	and	indicates	to	the financial	institution	that	the	funds	must	be	sent	immediately	to	pay	FinCEN	for	a	supposed “AML/CFT	violation,”	“outstanding	debt,”	or	a	“Treasury	grant.”
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-pattern urgent payment to a new payee under FinCEN "violation/debt" pretext (urgency-coercion scam)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.window: rolling 30 days per emerging payee relationship
build_logic.source: payment ledger + customer vulnerability segment + payee risk reference
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â fraud/AML & customer-protection review gate

indicators.flag: A	customer	indicates	that	they	received	a	phone	call,	text	message,	email,	or	U.S.	Mail	from FinCEN	demanding	immediate	payment.
indicators.red_flag: Customer reports a FinCEN "immediate-payment" demand via call/text/email/mail (imposter-contact tell)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D20 (External / lifestyle reference data (utilities, registries, merchant classification)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A	customer	presents	a	letter	supposedly	from	the	FinCEN	Director,	Deputy	Director,	or	any other	FinCEN	or	Treasury	official	requesting	immediate	payment.
indicators.red_flag: Customer presents a forged FinCEN/Treasury-official payment-demand letter (counterfeit-authority document)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D20 (External / lifestyle reference data (utilities, registries, merchant classification)), not currently held → source data first.
